title: They are his
hook: Ravana's own brother asks Rama for refuge, and the bhakti sutras end on why no devotee is ranked
carry: bhakti has no ranks: all who love are his
tomorrow: a king with everything asks to become one thing. what?

segments.voice: Yesterday, bhakti as a taste that can't be told, like a taste for someone who cannot speak, growing every moment.

On the shore across from Lanka, Rama's army watches a stranger come through the sky with four companions: Vibhishana, the demon king Ravana's own brother. He begged Ravana to give Sita back, was thrown out for it, and has come with nothing to offer but himself. Sugriva and others want him seized. Wrong family, wrong side, maybe a spy. Rama says no. In Valmiki's Ramayana he makes a vow: whoever comes to me even once, saying I am yours, I give safety from every being.
screen: `A STRANGER FROM LANKA.` → `WRONG FAMILY, WRONG SIDE.` → `I AM YOURS.`

segments.voice: The Narada Bhakti Sutras, which we finish today, name Vibhishana in their last pages among the teachers of love, next to Vyasa and Hanuman. Ravana's brother, listed as a master. That fits what the sutras say about the people of bhakti. When they talk together about the Lord, their throats choke, the hair on their arms stands up, and tears come. They make the holy places holier. And among them, the sutras say, there is no distinction of birth, learning, looks, family, wealth or work. Why? Tadiyah. Because they are his. That's one of Hinduism's big teachings, said plainly: in bhakti, belonging to God outranks everything else on the list. Family, degree, bank account: none of it sets your place. Rama on the shore is that line acted out. Then some advice. Don't lean on argument; it settles nothing. Read the books of love and do what wakes it up. Keep the plain virtues: not harming, truthfulness, purity, compassion, faith. And love, though one, takes eleven forms, among them love as a servant, a friend, a parent, a beloved, love that remembers, and the ache of being apart. Many teachers read that list as bhakti letting people come to God as they are. The book closes with a promise said twice: whoever trusts this teaching becomes a devotee and reaches the most beloved. Most of us rank people quietly, by school, job or family. The sutras say that in the house of love, those ladders aren't there.
screen: `RAVANA'S BROTHER, AMONG THE TEACHERS.` · `NO DISTINCTION: THEY ARE HIS.` · `ONE LOVE, ELEVEN FORMS.` · then, large: `BHAKTI HAS NO RANKS.`

segments.voice: Let the sutras' forms of love drift past slowly: a servant's, glad to help; a friend's; a parent's, watching over; a beloved's; love that remembers; love that aches when apart. Don't choose; notice which one warms a little as it passes, toward God if you pray, or toward a person you love if not, and stay with that one. Then, if you pray, say once the words Vibhishana brought to Rama: i am yours. If you don't, just stay with that person in mind.
Bhakti. In the last pages of the sutras, one love in eleven forms, and its people, among whom there is no distinction, because they are his.
Your line: bhakti has no ranks: all who love are his. Rama took in Ravana's own brother. That's the book, finished.

howItsDone: In devotional Hindu communities, the closing sutras are read as a portrait of the ideal devotee, and the forms of love they list, such as servant, friend, parent and beloved, are familiar ways of relating to God in bhakti traditions.

fork.reveal: Rama's vow: whoever comes even once saying 'i am yours' gets safety. the sutras later name Vibhishana among bhakti's teachers: no distinction, because they are his.

original.note: Sanskrit tadīyāḥ, 'they are his': the reason the sutras give for no distinctions among devotees.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, the arrival of Vibhishana and Rama's vow of refuge (sarga 18 in common editions)

notes: Last day of the Narada Bhakti Sutras block (1214–1219): the teach names the block's days and points to the Alvar hymns.

'Eleven forms' is stated because sutra 82 says it directly (ekādaśadhā). The script lists the forms in sutra 82's order, grouped; confirm the renderings (guṇa-māhātmya, rūpa, pūjā, smaraṇa, dāsya, sakhya, vātsalya, kāntā, ātma-nivedana, tanmayatā, parama-viraha).
Sutra 83's list of teachers is shortened to five names (Vyasa, Shandilya, Garga, Hanuman, Vibhishana) with 'among them'. Confirm.
Sutra 72 (no distinction of jāti, vidyā, rūpa, kula, dhana, kriyā) rendered 'birth, learning, looks, family, wealth or work'. Confirm.
Sutra 63 (on what not to listen to) and sutras 56–66 generally are not covered in this block.

The 'Six days' look-back counts the block (1214–1219), not a claim about the text. The close's claim that the tradition holds the Alvar hymns as 'love like this, sung aloud' is a bridge line; confirm it is fair.
